name: IRNSS-1A
reason: all three of its atomic clocks failed in 2016, so it cannot be used for navigation; IRNSS-1I replaced it in 2018
source: GPS World, 3 atomic clocks fail on 1 Indian satellite, https://www.gpsworld.com/3-atomic-clocks-fail-on-1-indian-satellite-replacement-prepped/; CelesTrak SATCAT 39199 (status P, partly operating), https://celestrak.org/satcat/records.php?CATNR=39199

name: NVS-02
reason: stranded in its transfer orbit (214 x 37,250 km) since its engine valves failed to open in February 2025, so it never reached its slot
source: GPS World, Indian navigation satellite stranded in transfer orbit, https://www.gpsworld.com/indian-navigation-satellite-stranded-in-transfer-orbit-after-valve-malfunction/; CelesTrak SATCAT 62850, https://celestrak.org/satcat/records.php?CATNR=62850

name: QZS-1 (Michibiki-1)
reason: replaced by QZS-1R in 2021 and moved above the geostationary belt (perigee 39,685 km); CelesTrak lists it as not operating, though the IGS file still gives it J01
source: Inside GNSS, QZSS replenishes 4-satellite constellation, https://insidegnss.com/qzss-replenishes-4-satellite-constellation-replacing-inaugural-michibiki/; CelesTrak SATCAT 37158 (status -), https://celestrak.org/satcat/records.php?CATNR=37158
